- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a significant price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 3–8% for the following 7-day horizon.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices; adjust forecast mean by subtracting 2–5% of recent 7-day average.
- Model underestimates volatility in late forecast windows (e.g., 25–30 days); increase forecast variance by 10–15% for horizon >20 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model tends to lag; shift forecast downward by 2–4% for next 3–5 days.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model exhibits “memory bias” — overweights recent highs; dampen forecast by 3–7% if last 5 days are above 85.
